metadata.description: One exploitability claim about one vulnerability in one software package version, as a Knowledge-family fact: the status, its justification, and the TestEvidence it rests on, all by reference. Knowledge, not a Resource: it is drafted by an analysis (a harness, a scanner, a person) and curated by Product Security; the intent record is the draft, the realized record is the confirmed statement. One vulnerability affects many packages, so VEX lives here, never on the Vulnerability record. ADOPT by reference (T5): OpenVEX 0.2.0 is the interchange shape and the source of the status codelist; the document is pointed at, not restated.

context.purpose: Records one exploitability claim about one vulnerability in one package version, with the evidence it rests on, as a fact Product Security can confirm.
context.plain_description: One statement per (vulnerability, package version). It carries the OpenVEX status (affected, not affected, fixed, under investigation), the standard's justification label when the status is not affected, the basis in plain words, and references to the tests that back it. A harness or a scanner drafts it (the intent record); Product Security confirms it (the realized record). It lives apart from the Vulnerability record because one vulnerability affects many packages.
use_when: An analysis has produced a draft exploitability claim that needs a reviewer before anyone relies on it.
A consumer or regulator asks what was verified about a known vulnerability in a shipped package.
An SBOM consumer needs the VEX status for a component and the evidence behind it.
